facts.text: Sherborn was settled in 1652 and incorporated in 1674, preserving rural heritage with farms, orchards, and over half the land as open space.
The town’s name originated when the General Court arbitrarily called it “Sherborne” before settling on Sherborn.
In the 1890s a local mill became advertised as the largest refined cider mill in the world, feeding Boston markets via stagecoach and later railroad.
Sherborn’s public library traces its roots to a 350‑year‑old story, celebrated with a digital archive launched for the town’s 350th birthday in 2024.
Sherborn shares a highly ranked public school system with neighboring Dover, and its elementary school is Pine Hill School.
The town sits 18 miles southwest of Boston, a short drive that lets residents enjoy both rural charm and easy access to the city.
